articles.title: World’s ‘largest’ grid battery part of Google-Xcel Energy agreement
articles.summary: Form Energy will supply iron-air batteries for the 300 MW/30 GWh deployment, which the parties say will bolster Xcel’s Upper Midwest grid with cost-effective multiday energy storage.

articles.title: EPA delays greenhouse gas reporting as it moves to shut down program
articles.summary: Covered entities for the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program will not be required to submit 2025 emissions data until October. By then, the agency may have repealed the requirement.

articles.title: Coal plant DOE ordered to stay online unlikely to run given ‘flush’ power supplies: CEO
articles.summary: The Department of Energy claimed “emergency” conditions in the Pacific Northwest required TransAlta to continue running Washington’s last coal plant past its planned retirement. The company plans to convert it to run on gas.

articles.title: Local control with reasonable county ordinances can support renewable energy deployment
articles.summary: The right regulations and permitting processes can help facilitate renewable resources facing county-level opposition, writes Claire Burch from the Oklahoma Renewable Energy Council.

articles.title: Utilities’ spending spree continues, according to their Q4 2025 reports
articles.summary: Companies highlighted their efforts to address affordability concerns through large load tariffs and other means when speaking about their fourth-quarter earnings.

articles.title: 600+ GWh of US energy storage expected by 2030: Benchmark/SEIA
articles.summary: The U.S. saw record battery deployments in 2025 and likely will again in 2026, propelled by utility-scale installations, according to a report prepared for the Solar Energy Industries Association.

articles.title: Declining solar, storage valuations drive increased M&A: Mercom
articles.summary: “When there is uncertainty, there are good deals to be had,” said Mercom CEO Raj Prabhu. “People are looking for late-stage, low-risk projects that are ready to go, and those are hot commodities.”

articles.title: The physics of reliability: Why gas peakers alone can’t save the modern grid
articles.summary: Most outages don’t start as a multihour energy shortage; they start as a frequency crisis. If you only have gas, you’re trying to stop a bullet with a shield that takes 10 minutes to lift, writes Arun Muthukrishnan from Arevon Energy.

articles.title: Data centers remain standout industry for Schneider Electric
articles.summary: Data center orders accelerated toward the end of 2025 and will likely remain strong through 2026 as projects planned for the next 18 to 24 months take shape, Schneider Electric Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said.

articles.title: Tariffs drove construction input prices up to start 2026
articles.summary: January’s cost increases amounted to a “blistering” annualized rate of 7.1% for nonresidential input prices, according to Associated Builders and Contractors. Copper was up 80% year over year, iron and steel 58% and switchgear 67%.

articles.title: Kairos, DOE enhance collaboration on advanced reactor design
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Kairos Power have entered into a USD27 million strategic partnership to accelerate the technology needed to deploy a new generation of advanced nuclear reactors.

articles.title: Reactor vessel installed at Lufeng 6
articles.summary: The reactor pressure vessel has been hoisted into place at unit 6 of the Lufeng nuclear power plant in China's Guangdong province. It is the second of two HPR1000 (Hualong One) units under construction at the site, where four CAP1000s are also planned.

articles.title: Contract signed for generic Polish BWRX-300 design
articles.summary: GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy and Orlen Synthos Green Energy have signed an agreement to develop a detailed technical design of the BWRX-300 small modular reactor adapted to Polish regulations, safety standards and environmental conditions.

articles.title: New heat-resistant steel developed for BR-1200
articles.summary: Rosatom says a new austenitic steel has been developed for the primary circuit of the planned lead-cooled BR-1200 reactor where the operating temperature will be 500-600 degrees Celsius.

articles.title: Lloyd's Register approves hybrid powered ship design
articles.summary: UK-based classification society and professional advisory service Lloyd's Register has issued approval in principle to Australian ship design group Seatransport Pty Ltd for a concept of a hybrid nuclear-diesel powered ship.

articles.title: Lithuania assessing potential for BWRX-300 deployment
articles.summary: Poland's SGE, Ignalina Nuclear Power Plant operator Altra and GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy have signed a memorandum of understanding to assess the potential for BWRX-300 small modular reactors in Lithuania.

articles.title: 'Transformative' research reactor mooted for Texas A&M
articles.summary: The Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station has signed an agreement with advanced small modular reactor company ZettaJoule to explore building a very-high temperature modular reactor that could attract USD1 billion in research funding.

articles.title: Potential sites identified for SMRs in Chernobyl exclusion zone
articles.summary: The State Agency of Ukraine for Exclusion Zone Management has said that sites by two long-abandoned villages have been identified as potential locations for future small modular reactors.

articles.title: First concrete for Kaiga 5 & 6 in India approved
articles.summary: India's Atomic Energy Regulatory Board has given its consent for the first pour of concrete for Kaiga units 5 and 6 - which are both 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors.

articles.title: Largest module installed at second Lufeng unit
articles.summary: The CA20 module - measuring about 20 metres in length, 14 metres in width and with a height of 21 metres - has been hoisted into place at the second unit of the Lufeng nuclear power plant in Guangdong province.

articles.title: First concrete poured for new capacity at Kaiga in India
articles.summary: The first pouring of concrete marks the point at which a project becomes a nuclear power unit under construction - the aim is for the first new unit at the Kaiga nuclear power plant to achieve criticality in five years.

articles.title: Potential for CANDU units in Turkey to be explored
articles.summary: Candu Energy and Türkiye Nuclear Energy Company have signed a memorandum of understanding to assess the potential for the deployment of Canadian CANDU reactor technology as Turkey looks to expand its nuclear energy capacity.

articles.title: South Korea to cooperate with the Philippines on nuclear power projects
articles.summary: Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power, the Export-Import Bank of Korea and the Philippines' largest private electric distribution utility Manila Electric Company have signed a tripartite memorandum of understanding for cooperation in developing nuclear power plants in the Philippines.

articles.title: Aalo secures fuel and turbine for experimental reactor
articles.summary: Aalo Atomics, a US developer of sodium-cooled small modular reactors for data centres, has signed a fuel fabrication contract with Global Nuclear Fuel. Meanwhile, Baker Hughes has been contracted to supply the steam turbine for Aalo-X, Aalo's experimental reactor.

articles.title: IAEA: Nuclear diplomacy is hard, but never impossible
articles.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency has urged restraint following the military attacks in Iran and the Middle East, and said it is ready to play its part in finding a diplomatic solution.

articles.title: Standard design approval sought for i-SMR
articles.summary: South Korea's Nuclear Safety and Security Commission has received an application for standard design approval for the Innovative Small Modular Reactor from the i-SMR Technology Development Project Group.

articles.title: Safety work planned for Chernobyl turbine hall
articles.summary: A contract has been signed for the development of detailed design documentation for work on parts of the turbine hall and deaerator stack that extend beyond the giant New Safe Confinement arch-shaped shelter which encloses the ruins of Chernobyl’s unit 4.

articles.title: TerraPower's Natrium reactor enters UK GDA process
articles.summary: The Bill Gates-chaired company's Natrium 345 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor with a molten-salt-based energy storage system has been accepted into the UK's Generic Design Assessment process.

articles.title: Philippines streamlines licensing for nuclear projects
articles.summary: The Philippine government has completed a "harmonised, whole-of-government licensing and permitting flowchart" for nuclear power plant projects, a key step toward enabling the safe and efficient operation of nuclear power facilities by 2032.

articles.title: Serbia and Russia discuss nuclear energy cooperation
articles.summary: Serbian Energy Minister Dubravka Đedović Handanović says that the country - already cooperating with France's EDF on the preparations for a nuclear energy programme - "is ready to establish cooperation with other technology providers from whom we can learn".
